POWER MECHANICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #8
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: POWER MECHANICS
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Before using a sharp tool in a workshop, you should: (1 mark)
   A. Work alone with eyes closed
   B. Wear safety gear and follow instructions
   C. Run with the tool
   D. Remove all guards

2. When learning Health and safety in a power mechanics work environment, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Health and safety in a power mechanics work environment.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Health and safety in a power mechanics work environment.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Health and safety in a power mechanics work environment.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Health and safety in a power mechanics work environment.

3. When learning Orthographic projection, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Orthographic projection.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Orthographic projection.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Orthographic projection.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Orthographic projection.

4. When learning ISO Thread forms, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for ISO Thread forms.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for ISO Thread forms.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after ISO Thread forms.
   D. Skip safety briefings for ISO Thread forms.

5. When learning Project, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Project.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Project.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Project.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Project.

6. When learning Metalwork processes in power mechanics, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Metalwork processes in power mechanics.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Metalwork processes in power mechanics.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Metalwork processes in power mechanics.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Metalwork processes in power mechanics.

7. A computer’s main brain for processing is the: (1 mark)
   A. Keyboard
   B. Speaker
   C. CPU
   D. Monitor

8. Electricity safety rule: (1 mark)
   A. Overload every socket
   B. Insert metal objects into sockets for fun
   C. Ignore burnt cables
   D. Never touch live wires with wet hands

9. When learning Braking system, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Braking system.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Braking system.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Braking system.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Braking system.

10. ICT stands for: (1 mark)
   A. International Cricket Team
   B. Internal Cooking Timer
   C. Input Cable Tester
   D. Information and Communication Technology

11. When learning Limits, fits and tolerance, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Limits, fits and tolerance.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Limits, fits and tolerance.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Limits, fits and tolerance.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Limits, fits and tolerance.

12. When learning Isometric projection, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Isometric projection.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Isometric projection.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Isometric projection.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Isometric projection.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Isometric projection and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Orthographic projection and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Limits, fits and tolerance and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain ISO Thread forms and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. B — Wear safety gear and follow instructions

2. D — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Health and safety in a power mechanics work environment.

3. B — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Orthographic projection.

4. A — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for ISO Thread forms.

5. A — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Project.

6. D — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Metalwork processes in power mechanics.

7. C — CPU

8. D — Never touch live wires with wet hands

9. D — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Braking system.

10. D — Information and Communication Technology

11. A — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Limits, fits and tolerance.

12. B — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Isometric projection.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Isometric projection; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Orthographic projection; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Limits, fits and tolerance; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of ISO Thread forms; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
